title: P-98 server half: activation events + the account-wide unlock-with-expiry read
missionPremise: OPS-16 amendment A-063 (2026-08-31) and _decisions/2026-08-31_next_action_rail_activation_engine.md. The Settings right rail becomes a next-action rail: one state-derived action, capability-first, able to go quiet, instrumented from the first commit. Two facts the ladder needs did not exist server-side. (1) An account-wide list of ACTIVE unlocks with expiry: hasPePropertyUnlock in peEntitlement.ts filters by parcelNodeId one parcel at a time, and the decision record names the expiring unlock as the highest-intent rung, so the read was in scope rather than deferred. (2) A PE-user-scoped activation event store: gtm_events is keyed on install_id for the browser extension and cannot answer a question about a signed-in account.
completionPredicate: GET /api/property-explorer/v1/entitlement/unlocks returns every active unlock for the signed-in account with its STORED expiry; POST /api/property-explorer/v1/activation-events writes one row to a new pe_activation_events table and REFUSES an unrecognised or absent event_type or action_id rather than defaulting; the monorepo typecheck is clean; artifacts/api-server test counts move only by the tests this lane added and no test regresses; artifacts/smartsite-mcp is byte-for-byte untouched and its counts are identical.
scopeBasis: Server half only, and both deliverables are ADDITIVE — no existing route, read or table changes behaviour. The hauska-map deep-allowlist is the client lane's item and was deliberately NOT edited: product repositories have one owning seat. The ladder component, the rung logic and the client's event emission are the client lane's (feat/p98-next-action-rail). Fixing the panel's 'Not read' / 'Not built' rows is out of scope for both halves per the client dispatch.

responses.200: { asOf: ISO, unlocks: [{ parcelNodeId, tenantId, unlockedAt: ISO, expiresAt: ISO|null, source }] }
responses.401: { error: 'authentication_required' } — NOT an empty list, which would claim 'you have unlocked nothing' about an account that was never identified
responses.500: { error: 'unlocks_unavailable' } — fails LOUD; an unreadable list must not degrade to an empty one, because a quiet rail is indistinguishable from an account with nothing expiring

deliverable1_unlocksRead.expiryIsStoredNotDerived: pe_property_unlocks.expires_at is a real nullable column (lib/db/src/schema/pePropertyUnlocks.ts). PE_PROPERTY_UNLOCK_DURATION_DAYS = 30 lives at artifacts/api-server/src/lib/pePaywallStripe.ts:44 and is WRITE-side only: the Stripe path computes now+30d and hands it to createPePropertyUnlock. No read derives from it and this one does not either. A NULL expires_at row (legacy / operator dev unlock) is ACTIVE but UNBOUNDED and ships as expiresAt: null; synthesising unlocked_at + 30 days would have the rail announce a lapse that does not exist.
deliverable1_unlocksRead.activePredicate: expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > asOf — copied verbatim from hasPePropertyUnlock so the list read and the per-parcel gate cannot disagree about the same row. One definition, not two.
deliverable1_unlocksRead.asOfRationale: The instant the ACTIVE predicate was evaluated at ships in the response. A consumer computing 'lapses in four days' then uses the same clock the filter used, so the countdown and the set cannot contradict each other, and no rounding rule had to be invented server-side.
deliverable1_unlocksRead.tenantNotUsedToNarrow: The primary key includes tenant_id, but the question is account-wide. Filtering by session tenant would silently hide unlocks bought under another and read as 'you have no unlocks'. tenantId is RETURNED per row instead.
deliverable1_unlocksRead.ordering: expires_at ASC (Postgres NULLS LAST on ASC, which is wanted: an unbounded unlock is the least urgent thing in the list), then parcel_node_id ASC as a stable tiebreak.

deliverable2_activationEvents.requestBody: { event_type: 'shown'|'acted', action_id: <closed set>, surface?: string }  (snake_case, matching the contract both P-98 dispatches state)

responses.201: { ok: true, event: { eventType, actionId, surface, createdAt } } — echoed from INSERT ... RETURNING, so createdAt is the database clock every later ratio buckets by, not a value this process guessed
responses.400: { error: 'invalid_event_type'|'invalid_action_id'|'invalid_surface', allowed?: [...] } — the refusal NAMES the vocabulary so a client/server drift explains itself
responses.500: { error: 'activation_event_not_recorded' } — the server always declares its failures; the client's silent drop is a deliberate degradation on that side only

ACTION_IDS_ARE_DEFINED_BY_THIS_LANE.why: Nothing in legacy-design-tools defined an action-id vocabulary before this work (grep verified 2026-08-31), and neither P-98 dispatch, OPS-16 A-063, nor the decision record names any id string. The server owns the closed set.
ACTION_IDS_ARE_DEFINED_BY_THIS_LANE.mapping: connect_claude = Account/Connections when pe_ai_connections shows none. unlock_expiring = Plan, an active unlock close to lapsing (the highest-intent rung, and the reason the unlock read was in scope). property_unlock = Plan, free tier with the chat allowance nearly exhausted. annual_upgrade = Plan, paid MONTHLY on solo or studio. team_invite = Team tier with unused seats, never any other tier.
ACTION_IDS_ARE_DEFINED_BY_THIS_LANE.COORDINATION_ITEM: The client lane must emit EXACTLY these strings. Any other id is a 400, which is the correct fail-closed direction but produces an empty funnel that would read as low engagement. This is surfaced rather than left to be discovered.

deliverable2_activationEvents.failClosedDesign: event_type and action_id are refused when unknown OR absent; nothing is defaulted. surface is nullable with NO default — gtm_events defaults source_surface to 'api', which invents an attribution, and an event whose surface was never sent is UNMEASURED, a different fact. A present-but-blank or non-string surface is refused rather than coerced to null, because coercing turns a client bug into an honest-looking absence and absence is a claim on this table.

migration.numberClaim: 0091. lib/db/drizzle holds 90 .sql files, highest 0090_pe_ai_connections.sql. The drizzle README requires checking open PRs AND unmerged branches because there is no meta journal and the FILENAME is the migration's identity: all six open PRs (554, 521, 510, 446, 445, 440) touch no lib/db/drizzle/00* file, and no unmerged remote branch claims a number at or above 0091. Positive determination, not an assumption.
migration.table: pe_activation_events (id uuid pk, owner_user_id text FK users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, event_type text, action_id text, surface text NULL, created_at timestamptz)
migration.namedFkConstraint: pe_activation_events_owner_user_id_users_id_fk — named explicitly so the SQL migration and drizzle-kit push produce ONE name. An inline unnamed REFERENCES gets Postgres's _fkey default while push names it _users_id_fk, and production would then differ from every test database by a string nobody looks at until it matters. Migration 0090 carries the same note.
checkConstraints: pe_activation_events_surface_chk CHECK (surface IS NULL OR surface <> '')
migration.theDeliberateAsymmetry: event_type is frozen in DDL because its grammar is closed at two values and is not expected to grow, so the check catches writers the TypeScript union never sees (a raw connection, a future job, a psql session). action_id is NOT a DDL value list because the ladder vocabulary grows once per rung, and a schema constraint would mean a new rung's events are refused until a migration lands — and because the client drops failed events on purpose, that loss would be SILENT, the exact failure this table exists to prevent. What is frozen for action_id is narrower and permanent: it may not be the empty string, the sentinel a plain NOT NULL admits. The reasoning is written into the migration header and the schema file, not only into this close.
migration.bypassNamed: A raw SQL connection can insert an unknown action_id. Today nothing else writes this table: the single writer is recordActivationEvent, reached only from the one route behind requirePeAuthenticated. If a second writer appears, that reasoning expires with it, and the writer module says so.
migration.beyondTheNamedShape: An `id uuid DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()` primary key was added, which the dispatch's named column list does not include. It mirrors gtm_events, the store this replaces; an append-only event log with no row identity cannot be deduped or referenced. Flagged here rather than made silently.

pe_activation_events inserted alphabetically. It sorts FIRST in the whole pe_ block: pe_ac < pe_ai (c < i) under ORDER BY tablename, so it lands between parcel_briefings and pe_ai_connections. The neighbouring comment on pe_ai_connections was corrected too, because it claimed pe_ai_connections sorts first in the pe_ block and that is no longer true.
hardcodedListsRefreshed.artifacts/api-server/src/__tests__/setup: pe_activation_events added to TRUNCATE_TABLES with the 'if a route writes to it, it's in this list' rationale. It cascades off users, but the activation suite asserts ROW COUNTS, so a leaked row from another test would silently break a refusal assertion.

schemaFixture.howThePatchWasCalibrated: From the committed fixture itself, not from memory of pg_dump behaviour. routeLevelCoverage.whatTheyAssert: Activation events: 401 writes nothing; 201 for each of the five action ids and both event types; surface stored NULL when absent (not 'api'); and EVERY refusal case additionally asserts ZERO ROWS IN THE TABLE, because a 400 body that says refused while a row lands anyway is invisible to a status-only assertion. LESSON: legacy-design-tools root `npx tsc --build` covers ONLY lib/* — root tsconfig.json has files: [] and references no artifacts/* project, and only lib/* set composite: true. Any verification phrased as 'tsc --build clean at root' is VACUOUS for artifacts/api-server, artifacts/smartsite-mcp and every other artifact. The real instrument is `pnpm run typecheck` (typecheck:libs then a per-artifact `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`), which is what CI runs. `npx tsc -b artifacts/<x>` also exits 0 while emitting nothing, because those projects are not composite — do not cite it either.

Hand-patching lib/db's schema.sql.template: calibrate from the committed file, never from memory of pg_dump. Three renderings verified there — drizzle `IN (...)` deparses to `= ANY (ARRAY['x'::text, ...])`; a string literal renders `''::text`; and pg_dump sorts CREATE TABLE constraints, PK blocks, INDEX blocks and FK blocks ALPHABETICALLY by name, not by creation order (county_facet_coverage's six checks prove it: dumped alphabetically, authored in a different order).

A new LDT table breaks THREE things, not the two usually named: the schema.integration.test.ts ORDER BY tablename list, the api-server setup.ts TRUNCATE list, AND the schema.sql.template fixture (4 separate blocks). Also check the neighbouring COMMENT in the integration list — inserting a table can falsify a comment that says which table sorts first in a block.

LDT migrations have NO drizzle meta journal; the FILENAME is the migration's identity. lib/db/drizzle/README.md requires scanning open PRs AND unmerged branches for the number before claiming it, because two branches shipping the same number collide when the second merges.

Put refusal/validation logic in a module that imports no database (the peAiConnectionsClassify precedent). In LDT, 163 of 316 api-server test files cannot collect without DATABASE_URL, so a refusal test written into a route suite is evidence only CI can run — which means nobody looks at it before merging.
